newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt slides lower, pins hopes on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German debt slides lower, pins hopes on U.S. data.

text.p: German debt started the Tuesday trading session on a weaker note and is likely to languish at still lower levels until the afternoon's U.S. data release, advertised as the session's potential highlight.
"What can I say, it is still very dull here with Bunds trading lower in very thin volume," said a Frankfurt-based trader, echoing several colleagues' comments.
Since opening with losses, the September Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange, has slipped some 19 basis points to 101.13, having traded in a range between 101.28 and 101.23.
Meanwhile the 10-year cash bond was trading at 101.76 after closing Monday's session at 101.97.

This morning's May German import prices, showing a 0.5 percent rise on the month and a 2.8 percent increase on the year, failed to jolt the market out of its slow slide, dealers said, adding more German state price data may also be ignored.

"If the (CPI) numbers come in more or less as expected, then German inflation data is not going to make much of an impact," another dealer said. Bavaria said on Monday that June prices climbed 0.2 percent on the month and 1.6 percent on the year, compared with May's 1.5 percent annual rise.

German states Baden Wuerttemberg, Hesse and North-Rhine Westphalia are scheduled to release their data in the next few days. This data then allows statisticians to calculate a preliminary West German inflation rate.

Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp is scheduled to speak at 1515 GMT, but market participants expect he, like several of his colleagues, will stress the need for a strong and stable common currency euro.
The session's highlight however is directed at this afternoon's U.S. May consumer confidence statistics, dealers said, adding this could invigorate trading again.
"We will have to see what happens in the U.S. and maybe that will be able to give us a bit of excitement," a dealer said.

Before the afternoon session however, Bunds are slated to trade between support at 101.09 and the 101.28 level. Resistance at 101.35 is not expected to be touched this morning, dealers said referring to generally low volumes.
